To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) privacy certificates can be automatically generated by the service provider; (2) the privacy certificates are machine readable; (3) they are based on the notion of privacy property; (4) the privacy certificates describe the privacy measures that are used to enforce a given privacy property; and (5) the privacy certificates can be checked against the privacy requirements of the client to select the services that are compliant with them.

1) a privacy certificate scheme can be designed and implemented in a privacy-aware service-oriented architecture; 2) the privacy certificates produced by the scheme can be used to select services whose privacy properties match the client policies; 3) a privacy certificate can be produced and managed by a certification authority (CA) and the service providers can be certified by the CA; 4) a privacy certificate contains a description of the privacy measures and the reasons why a certain privacy property holds for the service;
privacy certificates can be seen as the digital counterpart of privacy statements and that they provide the necessary support for the automated processing of privacy requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
(1) the formalization of the privacy certificates; (2) the definition of the certification process; (3) the development of a privacy-aware selection algorithm for web services.
the definition and the management of privacy certificates and their integration into a privacy-aware service architecture.
the definition of a privacy certificate scheme, the development of a prototype and the assessment of its feasibility.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

privacy certificates are a key element in the development of a machine-readable privacy framework for services, and can be used as a tool for the automation of privacy-aware processing of personal information.
privacy certificates are a promising instrument to support automated compliance checking, and to facilitate the development of privacy-aware services.
the privacy certification scheme we are proposing is an important step towards a fully automatic and privacy-aware processing of personal information on the web of (inter)connected services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
privacy certificates are a promising approach towards the development of privacy-aware services.
privacy certificates represent a novel approach towards the automatic processing of personal data, which can significantly contribute to the protection of privacy in the Web of Services.
the privacy certificates are the key enabler of a privacy-aware service selection process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
privacy certificates are a promising approach towards the development of a privacy-aware Web of Services.
a privacy certificate is a machine-readable document, which is used to describe a privacy property and its guarantees.
privacy certificates can be seen as a means to bridge the gap between privacy policies and the actual privacy guarantees provided by a service.
